skill.name: test-fixing
skill.description: Run tests, group failures by root cause, and apply focused fixes until the suite passes.
skill.summary: Systematically groups failing tests, fixes root causes, and verifies each repair.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Failing test suites can hide multiple root causes and waste review time. This skill groups failures, fixes high-impact causes first, and verifies each repair.
actual_capabilities: Runs the project test suite to collect current failures.
Groups failures by error type, file, and likely root cause.
Prioritizes infrastructure and API failures before assertion issues.
Applies minimal code changes that match project conventions.
Runs focused tests after each fix, then checks the full suite.
limitations: Assumes the repository has a working test command or clear test runner.
Cannot guarantee fixes when failures require missing services or secrets.
May need user guidance for flaky tests or ambiguous expected behavior.
Test execution can be slow on large projects.

use_cases.title: Recover After Refactors
use_cases.description: Group import, signature, and assertion failures after a code reorganization.

use_cases.title: Triage CI Failures
use_cases.description: Turn a failing CI log into ordered fix groups and verification steps.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Test Suites
use_cases.description: Work through recurring local failures with focused fixes and repeated checks.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Current Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a failing local suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the test suite, group the failures, fix the largest group first, and verify each change.

prompt_templates.title: Group CI Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using pasted CI failure details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CI failure output, identify shared root causes, and propose the safest fix order.

prompt_templates.title: Repair Refactor Regressions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after broad code movement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use recent changes and test output to fix refactor regressions with minimal edits and focused verification.

prompt_templates.title: Drive Full Stabilization
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for many unrelated failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Iterate through all failing test groups, explain each root cause, apply fixes, and finish with full-suite verification.

output_examples.input: The tests fail after a module rename.
output: Failures are grouped into import errors, signature mismatches, and assertion changes.
The import group is fixed first because it blocks many tests.
Focused checks pass before moving to the next group.
The report separates infrastructure failures from application logic failures.
Each group includes a likely cause, a planned fix, and a verification step.
The final status lists remaining failures, if any.

best_practices: Start with the full failure list before editing code.
Fix one root cause group at a time.
Run focused checks before the full suite.
anti_patterns: Changing unrelated code while chasing test failures.
Skipping verification after a partial fix.
Treating every failure as an independent problem.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the agent to run project test commands when the user asks for test repair.

faq.question: Can it handle pytest projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes focused pytest runs for individual files and matching failure patterns.

faq.question: Does it only work with Python?
faq.answer: No. The workflow applies to any project with readable test output and editable source files.

faq.question: How does it choose what to fix first?
faq.answer: It prioritizes groups that affect the most tests and unblock later failures.

faq.question: Can it fix flaky tests?
faq.answer: It can help investigate patterns, but intermittent behavior may require repeated runs and user judgment.

faq.question: Will it change production code or tests?
faq.answer: It makes the smallest focused change needed after identifying the likely root cause.
